decisions.question: OQ-R1: do the bus's subjects keep RxDart's microtask-delayed first delivery for state and replay topics, or wrap subjects so a new subscriber receives the current value synchronously?

options.label: keep the microtask-delayed first delivery
options.consequence: RxDart sync subjects give it natively (root D9); a listener's callback never runs before listen returns, as Dart stream code assumes; the synchronous first value is getCurrentValue or getBufferedValues; consumers must not render the replayed value twice

options.label: deliver the current value synchronously during listen
options.consequence: matches the Spec's 'replays immediately' literally, but needs subject code of nidana's own, breaks the Dart convention (late final sub = stream.listen(...) patterns fail), and buys nothing on a TestBus, which is deterministic either way (ADR-003 item 6)

decisions.chosen: keep the microtask-delayed first delivery
decisions.why: The atomicity rule of Spec §3.10 holds with RxDart's timing (the replay comes first, then the values delivered meanwhile, none missed); only 'immediately' is not synchronous. A synchronous delivery inside listen would need a custom Stream that violates what Dart stream consumers assume, and nidana.flutter already takes its first frame from getCurrentValue. Stated as G17; decides OQ-R1. The signal that would have changed it: a UI adapter that cannot read getCurrentValue before subscribing.

decisions.question: OQ-R3: where does StateTopic dedup sit, given the per-read opt-out of Spec §3.12, and does an observer see a publish that dedup suppressed?

options.label: dedup per read; observers and the current value see every publish
options.consequence: the subject sees every publish, so a Dedup.none read can see an equal one; every causation id a published envelope carries points at an envelope observers saw; telemetry also sees equal-value publishes

options.label: dedup at publish with a side channel for opted-out reads; observers see changes only
options.consequence: observers and recorders see fewer no-op publishes, but a Dedup.none read can publish an output whose cause no observer saw, breaking causation-chain walking through observed envelopes

decisions.chosen: dedup per read; observers and the current value see every publish
decisions.why: topology-dsl@v1 G19 already requires a Dedup.none read to see a publish equal to the current value, so the subject must receive every publish; the remaining choice was what observers see. Spec §3.7 has observers receive every publish event, and topic-model@v1 relies on every causation id pointing at an observed envelope. Stated as G16; decides OQ-R3. The signal that would have changed it: a telemetry cost profile where equal-value publishes dominate exported spans. Upstream: Spec §3.12 is silent on observers.
evidence: hsdd/contract/topic-model.md (How the lineage functions are applied)

decisions.question: How does the Interface make a publisher-less publish, and a publisher's publish, unable to reach a StateTopic, as Spec §2.4 requires?

options.label: amend topic-model@v1 with a sealed MultiWriterTopic<T> above EventTopic<T> and ReplayTopic<T>, and take it in publish
options.consequence: type-level: a state topic does not compile; the Spec's single publish(topic, value) shape survives; costs a compatible amendment of topic-model@v1 before bus-api@v1's fixtures compile

options.label: take Topic<T> and throw ArgumentError for a StateTopic
options.consequence: self-contained, no amendment, but the misuse surfaces at first run rather than at compile time, and the guarantee becomes a behavior case

options.label: one method per variant (publishEvent, publishReplay)
options.consequence: type-level without an amendment, but departs from the Spec's and the Guide's single publish name and doubles the surface

decisions.chosen: amend topic-model@v1 with a sealed MultiWriterTopic<T> above EventTopic<T> and ReplayTopic<T>, and take it in publish
decisions.why: Spec §2.4 says there is no publisher-less path to a StateTopic and that a publisher reaches one only through a writer handle; the owner's practice favors type-level proof (Rationale §3.3), and the step brief names this as a type-level reject fixture. Dart has no union types and topic-model@v1's Topic family is sealed, so only topic-model can declare the supertype. The amendment is compatible: switches over Topic stay exhaustive. Reject codes confirmed against a stand-in carrying it. If the amendment is declined, the fallback is the ArgumentError option, with no_publisherless_state_publish.dart and the first line of publisher_reaches_state_through_writer.dart turned into behavior cases.

decisions.question: Where is the boundary between bus-api@v1 and bus-testing@v1, given ADR-003's closed set of two providers and a TestBus that is a bus?

options.label: main library to bus-api, testing.dart to bus-testing, with SchedulerProvider sealed across both and Bus final with TestBus as its one subtype, declared in one src library
options.consequence: the closed provider set and 'TestBus is a Bus' hold by the language; bus-testing must declare its two types in the same implementation library as bus-api's

options.label: an open SchedulerProvider interface and an implementable Bus
options.consequence: simpler library layout, but applications could define providers that break the quiescence and cancellation rules (ADR-003 alternatives) and fake buses that bypass ordering and ownership

decisions.chosen: main library to bus-api, testing.dart to bus-testing, with SchedulerProvider sealed across both and Bus final with TestBus as its one subtype, declared in one src library
decisions.why: ADR-003 item 1 fixes exactly two providers; ADR-002 item 3 puts TestBus and the virtual scheduler in testing.dart. Dart's sealed and final are checked against the declaring library, so one src library with split exports gives both. BusConfig.scheduler is nullable so TestBus(config) can tell an unset provider from an explicit production one, which ADR-003 item 6 has it reject.

decisions.question: Is Bus an implementable interface (stand-ins, mocks) or a final class?

options.label: final class, TestBus its only subtype
options.consequence: no hand-written fake can bypass delivery, ordering or ownership; consumers test on a TestBus, as the Spec intends

options.label: abstract interface with a factory constructor
options.consequence: consumers could mock the bus with a mocking library before the runtime exists, at the cost of fakes that drift from the guarantees

decisions.chosen: final class, TestBus its only subtype
decisions.why: HSDD's rule is that the fixtures are the mocks, and Spec §3.6 and Appendix A.7 make TestBus the test substrate; every consumer in the tree has a hard edge on the real runtime or waits for its first phase (root D10). The signal that would have changed it: a consumer that must test against the bus before nidana.runtime's first phase merges.

decisions.question: How are dev-mode diagnostics typed so that other nidana packages can report through the bus's sink (root D8)?

options.label: sealed BusDiagnostic with final runtime variants plus a base ShellDiagnostic other packages extend, delivered through reportDiagnostic
options.consequence: the runtime's variants stay exhaustively switchable; navigation and Flutter add their own subclasses without touching bus-api

options.label: a closed sealed family only
options.consequence: exhaustive, but other packages could not report through the sink D8 says they read

options.label: an open interface
options.consequence: anyone can add variants, so no consumer can switch exhaustively

decisions.chosen: sealed BusDiagnostic with final runtime variants plus a base ShellDiagnostic other packages extend, delivered through reportDiagnostic
decisions.why: Root D8 says every nidana package with dev-mode behavior reads dev mode and the sink from the bus it holds, and that diagnostics are values of a sealed type. A sealed base with one base-class extension point gives both; reportDiagnostic does nothing outside dev mode so callers need not check. Diagnostics carry no payload, so nothing needs redaction (Spec §9.2 item 2).

decisions.question: What do the throws the Specification requires look like on Dart?

options.label: a sealed BusError family (ActivationRejected, ClaimRejected, TopologyConflict, TopicCollision, BusLimitExceeded) carrying findings, plus SDK ArgumentError and StateError for misuse
options.consequence: callers and tests match on typed causes with topology-ir@v1's findings attached; removeTopic returns false rather than throwing when refused

options.label: SDK errors only (StateError, ArgumentError)
options.consequence: smaller surface, but a caller cannot tell a cycle from a writer conflict without parsing messages

decisions.chosen: a sealed BusError family (ActivationRejected, ClaimRejected, TopologyConflict, TopicCollision, BusLimitExceeded) carrying findings, plus SDK ArgumentError and StateError for misuse
decisions.why: Spec §3.11 has the rejection name the current owner, which the WriterConflict finding carries; root D8 keeps these as throws. They extend Error because each is a configuration bug the CI checks should have caught. Spec §7.5 lets removal return false per platform convention, which reads naturally in Dart.

decisions.question: How is reentrant publish normalization realized: which publishes are reentrant, and how are deferred publishes ordered?

options.label: a publish made during a delivery joins one per-bus FIFO drained by one provider-zone microtask, including the publishes the drain itself causes; timer-driven publishes are not reentrant
options.consequence: fan-out emissions stay consecutive with no intervening publish (Spec §3.3); a delivery of a publish is the unit of reentrancy

options.label: one scheduleMicrotask per reentrant publish, as Spec §3.4's table reads
options.consequence: simplest, but a microtask some subscriber schedules can run between two emissions of one fan-out

options.label: defer every publish while the queue is non-empty
options.consequence: call order equals delivery order even across shell publishes, but a shell publish becomes asynchronous whenever anything is pending

decisions.chosen: a publish made during a delivery joins one per-bus FIFO drained by one provider-zone microtask, including the publishes the drain itself causes; timer-driven publishes are not reentrant
decisions.why: Spec §3.3 promises fan-out in declaration order with no intervening external publishes, and Spec §3.4 normalizes reentrant publishes to the next scheduling boundary. One FIFO drained in one microtask satisfies both, avoids RxDart's same-subject StateError and depth-first delivery (root D9), and makes publishes made in sequence consecutive (G14), which the navigation executor's paired writes rely on (Guide §3.4).

decisions.question: What does the startup barrier hold back: only shell publishers' publishes, as Spec §3.13 words it, or every publish?

options.label: every publish, a topology's and a publisher-less one included; the connection and observed first values are not publishes and are not held
options.consequence: nothing reaches a subscriber or an observer before start, so activation order before start is irrelevant for every variant (Rationale §3.1)

options.label: shell publishers' publishes only
options.consequence: the literal wording, but a topology's output from its connection would be delivered before start and an APPLICATION reader activated later could miss it

decisions.chosen: every publish, a topology's and a publisher-less one included; the connection and observed first values are not publishes and are not held
decisions.why: Spec §3.13 says nothing is delivered before start and that activation order is irrelevant for APPLICATION topologies; the only topology publishes before start come from activation connections, and holding them back is what makes the order irrelevant (G34 runs both orders and compares). Upstream: Spec §3.13 should say every publish is queued.

decisions.question: Spec §3.9: when is a second activation under the same topologyId 'the same declaration', given that definitions do not see a scan seed, closure bodies or two functions with one name?

options.label: equal topology-ir@v1 definitions are the same declaration; declare runs once more for the check
options.consequence: the DI double-registration case returns the same handle; differences the IR cannot see are not detected

options.label: the same Topology object (identity)
options.consequence: detects nothing new, and turns two instances of one topology class, the motivating case, into an error

options.label: equal definitions and the same runtime type
options.consequence: catches two classes with one id and equal wiring, but the builder form has one runtime type for every topology

decisions.chosen: equal topology-ir@v1 definitions are the same declaration; declare runs once more for the check
decisions.why: The bus can compare only what the IR records; Dart cannot compare closures. Spec §3.9's motivation is one topology registered twice, usually as two instances. Stated as G23 with the limitation spelled out and a case that shows two scan seeds sharing a handle. The signal that would have changed it: a reported bug where two different closures under one id silently shared a handle. Upstream: Spec §3.9 should say observable differences are judged on the IR.

decisions.question: Spec §4.3's runtime name check throws on 'a different type'. Does a second declaration of the same name and type that differs in its sensitive flag, tracing, dedup or buffer size collide?

options.label: collide on variant, value type, sensitive, tracing, dedup or buffer size
options.consequence: a second declaration that drops the sensitive flag cannot share a subject and leak envelopes to non-sensitive observers

options.label: collide on variant and value type only
options.consequence: the literal rule; equal topics (topic-model@v1 G7) with different flags would share one subject, and the flag on each envelope would depend on which declaration published it

decisions.chosen: collide on variant, value type, sensitive, tracing, dedup or buffer size
decisions.why: envelope.sensitive comes from the topic object used at the publish (MessageEnvelope.publishedTo), so two declarations differing in the flag would mix sensitive and non-sensitive envelopes on one subject, which Spec §9.2's gating cannot recover from. Upstream: Spec §4.3 should name the declaration fields.

decisions.question: How do maxTopics (Spec §11.3, 'activate fails if exceeded') and getCurrentValue's 'never throws' (Spec §2.5) combine?

options.label: activation over the limit throws BusLimitExceeded; any other access over it creates the subject and reports TopicLimitExceeded in dev mode
options.consequence: getCurrentValue keeps its never-throws rule; a topic-creating loop still shows up, in dev mode and at the next activation

options.label: every subject creation over the limit throws
options.consequence: a hard cap everywhere, contradicting Spec §2.5 for getCurrentValue

decisions.chosen: activation over the limit throws BusLimitExceeded; any other access over it creates the subject and reports TopicLimitExceeded in dev mode
decisions.why: Spec §11.3 names activation only, and Spec §2.5 forbids getCurrentValue from throwing; the diagnostic keeps the guardrail visible. getCurrentValue still throws TopicCollision, which Spec §4.3 requires. The limit defaults are the Spec §11.3 example values. Upstream: the Spec should say how the cap and getCurrentValue interact.

decisions.question: Does a shell publish carry causation, as Spec §2.4's PaymentResult example suggests, or is it always a root message?

options.label: always a root message: fresh correlation, no causation
options.consequence: matches Guide §3.6 (a page's publish is a root publish); shell code never needs envelopes; a service's result is not linked to the intent that prompted it

options.label: link it to the delivery in progress through an ambient context
options.consequence: reconstructs the Spec's example chain for synchronous handlers, but async work loses the context and every delivery would need a zone or a stack

options.label: an explicit causedBy argument on publish
options.consequence: precise, but shell code would need envelopes, which observed streams do not carry

decisions.chosen: always a root message: fresh correlation, no causation
decisions.why: Guide §3.6 states that the bus does not link a page's publish to the intent that opened it, and Guide §10.2 lists that link as an open observability convenience. Observed streams carry payloads only (Refinement 4). Listed under Versioning as a candidate for a later version.

decisions.question: What does Tracing.disabled do on this bus?

options.label: its envelopes reach no observer and a pipeline reading it starts a new flow; the envelopes still carry generated metadata
options.consequence: the observable rule of Guide §8.1 holds; the TestBus recorder can still show untraced values with ids, which topology-dsl@v1's live G25 case needs

options.label: placeholder metadata (empty ids, no timestamp)
options.consequence: saves id generation and a clock read, but no allocation, because a Dart envelope holds its payload

decisions.chosen: its envelopes reach no observer and a pipeline reading it starts a new flow; the envelopes still carry generated metadata
decisions.why: Spec §3.5 Cost describes a singleton untracked envelope; in Dart the envelope holds the payload, so no allocation is saved. topic-model@v1 fixes the lineage rule and S06 noted observers must not see untraced envelopes; the live suite watches an untraced topic and compares its correlation id.

decisions.question: What shape does the module scope API that UI adapters bind route events to take (Spec §7.3)?

options.label: bus.module(id, topologies, gracePeriod) returning one ModuleScope per id; acquire() returns a ModuleReference token whose release counts once
options.consequence: double releases from route lifecycles cannot drive the count negative; a failed activation leaves the count at zero

options.label: acquire() and release() counters on the scope
options.consequence: smaller surface, but a duplicated release silently tears the module down

options.label: an id-less scope object held by the adapter
options.consequence: no registry, but two widgets of one module subtree would keep separate counts

decisions.chosen: bus.module(id, topologies, gracePeriod) returning one ModuleScope per id; acquire() returns a ModuleReference token whose release counts once
decisions.why: Spec §7.3 makes reference counting the only correct pattern and warns about double mount and unmount in React StrictMode; tokens make release idempotent per reference. Modules take module-scoped topologies only (Spec §7.2). The signal that would have changed it: flutter-binding@v1 needing to release without holding the reference.

decisions.question: Spec §2.4: 'a publisher bound to a module or page scope releases it with that scope'. Does bus-api@v1 bind publishers to module scopes?

options.label: no: scope is declared on the publisher for the analyses, and the caller disposes it when it releases the module or the page unmounts
options.consequence: no lifecycle surface without a consumer; a page adapter disposes its publishers itself

options.label: ModuleScope.publisher(...) disposed at module teardown
options.consequence: automatic release, but the shell component would hold a publisher that dies after the grace period and must obtain a new one on re-entry

decisions.chosen: no: scope is declared on the publisher for the analyses, and the caller disposes it when it releases the module or the page unmounts
decisions.why: Every shell-owned state topic Spec §3.11 lists (executor, connectivity, location, permissions, migration bridge) is application-level; nidana.flutter owns page publishers and disposes them on unmount. Listed under Versioning as a candidate. The signal that would have changed it: a module or page that claims a state topic.

decisions.question: Is the SDK-neutral telemetry observer (root D1) part of bus-api@v1, and how does it see activations when BusObserver has only onPublish?

options.label: TelemetryObserver in the main library, plus an ActivationObserver interface the bus also notifies
options.consequence: the full Guide §8.2 mapping, activation spans included, without touching topic-model@v1's BusObserver

options.label: TelemetryObserver with publish spans only
options.consequence: no new interface, but the Guide's activation row is dropped

options.label: add onActivate to BusObserver
options.consequence: one interface, but a breaking change to topic-model@v1, which applications implement

decisions.chosen: TelemetryObserver in the main library, plus an ActivationObserver interface the bus also notifies
decisions.why: Root D1 puts the observer in nidana.runtime's main package and its public surface needs a contract; Guide §8.2 maps both publishes and activations onto spans. Attribute keys follow the Guide's nidana.sensitive in snake case under one nidana. prefix; spans are opened and ended within the call, since an observer has no clock.
evidence: hsdd/contract/topic-model.md (Versioning: adding a member to BusObserver is breaking)

decisions.question: Spec §7.2 says the bus enforces that APPLICATION topologies activate before start(). Does a later APPLICATION activation throw?

options.label: report LateApplicationActivation in dev mode and activate
options.consequence: the symptom shows in debug and test runs; a test that activates after start is not failed on a scope it does not exercise

options.label: throw StateError
options.consequence: strict enforcement, at the cost of every after-start activation of an APPLICATION topology, in apps and tests alike

options.label: nothing
options.consequence: silent; the activation-order hazard of Spec §3.13 goes unnoticed

decisions.chosen: report LateApplicationActivation in dev mode and activate
decisions.why: No evidence settles it. The diagnostic surfaces the hazard Spec §3.13 exists to prevent while keeping the operation total. The signal that would have changed it: the owner preferring hard enforcement, which is a compatible tightening only before v1 is stable.

decisions.question: What happens to a publish that is queued (before start, or reentrant) when its publisher is disposed or its topology deactivated?

options.label: discard it
options.consequence: a released owner's state publish can never land after a new claimant's (Spec §3.11); a service that publishes and disposes before start loses that publish

options.label: deliver it
options.consequence: every publish call is honored, but a queued state publish could be delivered after another claimant took the topic

decisions.chosen: discard it
decisions.why: Single-writer ownership is structural (Spec §3.11, Rationale §2.1); delivery after release would allow a second writer's value to interleave with the old owner's. topology-dsl@v1 G29 says a deactivated topology publishes nothing afterwards; discarding makes that hold for what subscribers observe.

decisions.question: ADR-003 left open whether shutdown() drains the virtual queue first. What does shutdown do with pending work?

options.label: deliver the bus's own pending reentrant publishes synchronously, discard the startup queue, run nothing else of the provider zone
options.consequence: works the same on both providers, needs no scheduler operation, and honors 'drains pending dispatches'

options.label: discard every pending publish
options.consequence: simplest, but drops publishes already made

options.label: run the virtual scheduler's triggerActions first on a TestBus
options.consequence: drains more on a TestBus, but behaves differently from the production provider and makes bus-api depend on bus-testing

decisions.chosen: deliver the bus's own pending reentrant publishes synchronously, discard the startup queue, run nothing else of the provider zone
decisions.why: Spec §11.2 says shutdown drains pending dispatches; ADR-003 requires shutdown not to chain on futures, and the bus's FIFO of reentrant publishes is its own, so it can be drained synchronously. Publishes queued before start were never dispatched. What a TestBus does beyond that is bus-testing@v1's.

decisions.question: ADR-003 left open whether a TestBus generates deterministic envelope ids. What does bus-api@v1 say?

options.label: ids and correlation ids are opaque and pairwise distinct; whether a TestBus makes them deterministic is bus-testing@v1's
options.consequence: bus-api's suite compares ids only by reference to observed envelopes; bus-testing@v1 decides golden-friendly ids

options.label: fix an id format here
options.consequence: deterministic ids for every bus, at the cost of fixing a production format no consumer needs

decisions.chosen: ids and correlation ids are opaque and pairwise distinct; whether a TestBus makes them deterministic is bus-testing@v1's
decisions.why: No bus-api guarantee depends on an id's value, and the TestBus is bus-testing@v1's declaration; a deterministic scheme can be an internal hook of the package.

decisions.question: How does the bus-api conformance harness let a case drive time without naming bus-testing@v1 types?

options.label: BusApiHarness with bus(config), flush, advance, pendingTimers and settle, all in bus-api and SDK types; production-provider capture tested by constructing a Bus inside a TestBus delivery
options.consequence: the library compiles against bus-api alone; the binding maps the calls to TestBus and its scheduler

options.label: let the library import testing.dart
options.consequence: fewer indirections, but the suite would not compile until bus-testing@v1 lands and could not bind any other virtual implementation

decisions.chosen: BusApiHarness with bus(config), flush, advance, pendingTimers and settle, all in bus-api and SDK types; production-provider capture tested by constructing a Bus inside a TestBus delivery
decisions.why: The step brief requires it, and ADR-001 item 4 has a harness supply factories and settle. A delivery runs in the provider zone, so a Bus constructed there captures the virtual zone and clock, which tests ADR-003 item 1 without package:clock in a fixture.

decisions.question: How does the binding of topology-dsl@v1's live suite implement LiveRun.watch, which must return envelopes, including those of a Tracing.disabled topic?

options.label: a view of the TestBus's envelope recorder from the watch on, filtered to the topic and read with its own dedup
options.consequence: works for every topic; forward-references bus-testing@v1's recorder and requires it to record untraced topics

options.label: a BusObserver per watch
options.consequence: uses bus-api only, but observers never see an untraced topic (G30), so the live G25 untraced case fails

options.label: make publish return its envelope
options.consequence: adds surface to bus-api for one binding, and still misses envelopes topologies publish

decisions.chosen: a view of the TestBus's envelope recorder from the watch on, filtered to the topic and read with its own dedup
decisions.why: The live suite's untraced case watches a Tracing.disabled topic and reads its envelope's correlation id; observers cannot see it by design, and Spec §3.5 lists the TestBus recorder as an envelope-visible party. The experiment's seeded defect (a recorder that drops untraced topics) fails that case, which makes the requirement on bus-testing@v1 explicit.

decisions.question: Forced removal and shutdown must end observed subscriptions with done; a closed RxDart BehaviorSubject delivers done from a microtask the virtual scheduler does not run. What does the contract guarantee?

options.label: the bus ends every observed subscription itself, with done delivered before removeTopic or shutdown returns
options.consequence: deterministic on every provider; the runtime wraps each observed subscription

options.label: done follows the subject's close, whenever the engine delivers it
options.consequence: no wrapper, but on a TestBus done needs a real event-loop turn, which ADR-003 item 6 rules out for anything a bus operation schedules

decisions.chosen: the bus ends every observed subscription itself, with done delivered before removeTopic or shutdown returns
decisions.why: output-close.txt shows a sync BehaviorSubject delivering done from a microtask while PublishSubject, ReplaySubject and sync controllers deliver it synchronously; the stand-in's G9 case failed after a flush until the bus closed its own per-subscription controllers. Stated in G9, G18 and G36.

decisions.question: Which assignments does the immutability reject fixture pin, given that assigning a getter reports assignment_to_final for a final field and assignment_to_final_no_setter for a getter without one?

options.label: BusConfig's fields only, which its const constructor makes final
options.consequence: the reject code does not depend on how the producer implements Bus's getters

options.label: Bus's and Publisher's getters too
options.consequence: wider coverage, but the expected code would depend on the producer's choice of fields or getters, a fixture gap the first replay would surface

decisions.chosen: BusConfig's fields only, which its const constructor makes final
decisions.why: The probe against the stand-in showed bus.clock = ... reporting nothing for a late final field and assignment_to_final for a final one; topology-ir@v1 recorded the same ambiguity. A const constructor requires final fields, so BusConfig's code is stable.

decisions.question: Dev-mode recursion detection (Spec §3.4): what happens past maxReentrancyDepth?

options.label: report ReentrancyDepthExceeded once per chain, at the hop that crosses the threshold, and keep delivering
options.consequence: dev and release builds deliver the same values; a runaway loop shows as a diagnostic and, on a TestBus, as the scheduler's action bound

options.label: stop delivering the chain in dev mode
options.consequence: a loop cannot starve the event loop in debug builds, but dev mode would change what the app does

decisions.chosen: report ReentrancyDepthExceeded once per chain, at the hop that crosses the threshold, and keep delivering
decisions.why: Spec §3.4 asks for detection and a diagnostic with the chain, not for interruption; ADR-003 item 5's action bound already surfaces a runaway loop on a TestBus.

decisions.question: Where do observers' log, metric and span calls go?

options.label: one ObserveContext per bus in BusConfig, defaulting to a context whose log prints and whose metric and span discard
options.consequence: an app plugs its telemetry backend in once; a logging observer prints out of the box

options.label: a context per observer at addObserver
options.consequence: different sinks per observer, which no v1 consumer needs

options.label: a default that discards everything
options.consequence: silent by default; a logging observer added without a context shows nothing

decisions.chosen: one ObserveContext per bus in BusConfig, defaulting to a context whose log prints and whose metric and span discard
decisions.why: Spec §3.7 gives observers out-of-band sinks without saying who supplies them; the OpenTelemetry binding is deferred (root D1), so the app supplies the sinks. No evidence beyond judgement; the signal that would have changed it: two observers needing different backends.

decisions.question: Does the runtime's main library re-export nidana_dart_contracts?

options.label: no; shell code imports both
options.consequence: each import names its package and version; consistent with topology_ir.dart not re-exporting the main contracts library

options.label: yes
options.consequence: one import for apps, at the cost of the runtime's namespace carrying every contracts declaration

decisions.chosen: no; shell code imports both
decisions.why: Judgement and consistency with topology-ir@v1's library rule; nothing in the Spec or ADR-002 asks for re-export. Compatible to add later.

experiments.question: Do bus-api@v1's fixtures hold together before the producer exists: does every reject fixture report exactly its marked codes, does the surface set analyze clean, do the bus-api suite and topology-dsl@v1's live suite pass against an implementation of the Interface on RxDart 0.28, and do they fail when the implementation is broken?
experiments.finding: With a stand-in topic model carrying the proposed MultiWriterTopic and a stand-in runtime on RxDart 0.28 sync subjects: structure PASS for all 39 guarantees (86 cases, 2 bindings, 14 fixture files); surface clean; all 8 reject files PASS with their (line, code) pairs; the bus-api suite passes 86 of 86 and the live suite 43 of 43 on a stand-in TestBus; 38 seeded defects in the stand-in each fail the cases of the guarantee they break (T10), 4 seeded defects fail live cases (T11), including a recorder that drops untraced topics; adding a BusDiagnostic variant fails the surface set (T12).

experiments.question: When does done reach a subscriber of a closed RxDart sync subject or sync controller?
experiments.finding: PublishSubject, ReplaySubject and sync StreamControllers deliver done synchronously inside close(); a sync BehaviorSubject delivers it from a microtask, which a virtual scheduler's flush did not run, so the bus must end observed subscriptions itself (G9, G18, G36).

experiments.question: Which diagnostic does each candidate type-level misuse of the Interface report?
experiments.finding: Final and sealed types report invalid_use_of_type_outside_library; an implements of a final class needs abstract to avoid non_abstract_class_inherits_abstract_member on the same line; a variant mismatch adds inference_failure_on_function_invocation unless the type argument is explicit; a set literal of the wrong topic variant reports set_element_type_not_assignable; assigning a late final field reports nothing, so assignment rejects are pinned to BusConfig.

notes_for_orchestrator: Boundary with bus-testing@v1 (S10): bus-api@v1 is the main library; bus-testing@v1 is testing.dart. SchedulerProvider is sealed across both (VirtualSchedulerProvider declared by bus-testing@v1 in the same src library, exported only by testing.dart); Bus is final with TestBus as its only subtype, declared in the same src library; BusConfig.scheduler is nullable so TestBus(config) gives a fresh virtual provider for null, uses a VirtualSchedulerProvider, and rejects ProductionSchedulerProvider with ArgumentError (ADR-003 item 6).

S10 must provide, or rewrite the two bus-api bindings' calls to its own names (no case changes): TestBus([BusConfig config]); TestBus.scheduler (VirtualScheduler) with void triggerActions(), void advanceTimeBy(Duration), int get pendingTimerCount, Future<void> settle(); TestBus.recorder.envelopes, a List<RecordedEnvelope> (TopicRef topic, MessageEnvelope<Object?> envelope) of every envelope delivered on the bus, Tracing.disabled topics included, in delivery order, recorded at delivery before observers; a fresh VirtualScheduler constructed in the zone current at TestBus construction (the G18 case constructs the TestBus inside runZonedGuarded). The orchestrator must let S10 edit hsdd/contract/fixture/bus-api/behavior/{nidana_dart_runtime_test,bus_activation_test}.dart, or schedule a bus-api fixture amendment, if S10 chooses other names.

Left to S10 with reasons recorded: deterministic TestBus ids (bus-api states ids opaque and distinct); the recorder's assertion API and sensitive-payload redaction default (Spec §9.2 item 2; the live binding reads only non-sensitive envelopes); the settle bound; the fixed start instant; OQ-R2. S10 can reuse docs/auto-run/experiments/bus-api-fixtures/packages/nidana_dart_runtime/lib/src/testing.dart as a starting stand-in.

OQ-R1 decided by G17: observed subscriptions keep RxDart's microtask-delayed first delivery for state and replay topics; the synchronous first value is getCurrentValue/getBufferedValues. OQ-R3 decided by G16: dedup per read; the subject, the current value and observers see every publish, an equal one included. Both rows in hsdd/spec/nidana.runtime.md are owned by that node; the runtime's decomposition step marks them RESOLVED pointing at bus-api@v1 G17 and G16.

Amendment needed (compatible) on topic-model@v1 before bus-api@v1's Interface and fixtures compile: add `sealed class MultiWriterTopic<T> extends Topic<T>` with EventTopic<T> and ReplayTopic<T> extending it (no public constructor; switches over Topic stay exhaustive), plus a guarantee and its surface/reject fixture in topic-model's set. The stand-in shape is docs/auto-run/experiments/bus-api-fixtures/packages/nidana_dart_contracts/lib/src/topic_model.dart. Fallback if declined: Bus.publish and Publisher.publish take Topic<T> and throw ArgumentError for a StateTopic; no_publisherless_state_publish.dart and line 15 of publisher_reaches_state_through_writer.dart become behavior cases. No change is needed to topology-dsl@v1 or topology-ir@v1.

S11 (navigation-api@v1): the executor claims nav.current-route with bus.publisher(ExecutorSource(name), writes: {currentRoute}), writes it through publisher.writer(currentRoute), publishes history through publisher.publish (a ReplayTopic), subscribes with bus.observe(resolvedIntent) (payloads, first value rules of G17), stamps RouteTransition.timestamp with bus.clock.now(), registers its dispose with bus.onShutdown, and reports dev-mode problems as a ShellDiagnostic subclass through reportDiagnostic. G14 makes the paired currentRoute and history publishes consecutive whether or not they are reentrant (Guide §3.4); G34 covers the deep-link bootstrap order (Guide §3.5).

S12 (flutter-binding@v1): BusProvider holds a Bus; a topic widget takes its first frame from getCurrentValue and must not render the first observed value twice (it equals the value current at listen, G17); page publishers use PageSource and are disposed by the adapter on unmount (no module or page binding of publishers in v1); page scope is activate/deactivate on mount/unmount; module scope is bus.module(id, topologies) once per module plus acquire()/ModuleReference.release() per route, the grace timer running in the provider zone so tester.pump drives it with a production-provider bus built in the test body; shutdown is synchronous and leaves no timer (G36, ADR-003 item 7); adapter diagnostics extend ShellDiagnostic.

nidana.tooling (surface only): a claim is the Bus method publisher in package nidana_dart_runtime with source as first positional argument, writes and scope as named arguments; match package and element names, never the declaring library path (it is under lib/src/). Bus declares no static accessor.

Runtime decomposition: the contract is too large for one leaf-parent's behavior but not for one skeleton phase. Recommended: one child owns lib/nidana_dart_runtime.dart and lands every declaration of bus-api@v1 (and the src library holding Bus, TestBus and the provider family, shared with bus-testing@v1) in its first phase, with bodies throwing UnimplementedError; that phase must precede every other producing phase, so ADR-001 item 10's full surface and reject replay holds at every producing phase of every child. Behavior then splits by --guarantee, for example: registry and publish path G6 to G18; ownership and activation G19 to G26 and G37 plus bus_activation_test.dart; module scopes, barrier and shutdown G27, G28, G34 to G36; observation and diagnostics G4, G29 to G33; time source G5 with bus-testing@v1. If the decomposition instead gives several children their own public declarations, ADR-001 item 10 needs an amendment scoping surface and reject per file.

Upstream candidates recorded (would_upstream): Spec §2.1/§7.4 'replays immediately' on engines with asynchronous first delivery (G17); Spec §3.12 silent on observers (G16); Spec §3.13 should say every publish is queued (G34); Spec §3.9 equality judged on the IR (G23); Spec §4.3 declaration fields in the collision check (G7); Spec §2.5 and §11.3 interplay (G10).
